label: no
controls_available: Full direct manipulation: wheel-scroll each linked slice canvas to change its orthogonal slice focus.
Drag empty mesh glass to orbit the reconstruction.
Drag from one visible mesh node to another to add a merge.
Click visible slice nodes to place the active red or green split seed.
Click CUT BETWEEN SEEDS to remove a false join.
Click CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH to submit.
The environment declares mouse and keyboard actions, but this mechanic installs no task-specific keyboard handler; the full surface is mouse, pointer, and wheel driven.
autonomous_processes: None: after rendering, the Branch Repair nodes, edges, slice focus, camera, seeds, and controls remain unchanged until a native scroll, drag, click, or certification event. The generic live task clock can advance, but this mechanic neither reads it nor uses it to mutate task state.
grouped_control_modes: D_full: the full direct-manipulation repair surface across all level-1 seeds, attempts, and repair occurrences; it includes slice scrolling, mesh orbit/merge drags, slice seed placement, cutting, and certification.

clause_i.reason: An observation-free wait/no-op policy remains compatible with an optimal eventual continuation for every history because waiting causes no task-state change and no repair opportunity expires; the source provides no autonomous transition that would make the next action depend on visible evolution.

clause_ii.reason: A zero-length bounded window is sufficient in the limited sense that the current static screenshot exposes the current canvases and direct controls, and the observation-free wait/no-op policy is itself a valid delayed-optimal choice. No temporal evidence is needed to predict a changed state.

clause_iii.reason: There is no autonomous H_t to H_t^tau evolution while the agent supplies no action. Branch Repair changes only inside scroll, orbit, seed, merge, split, or submit handlers; the grader has no time advancement or deadline logic. Consequently no available outcome-affecting action becomes unavailable or strictly less effective for any Delta > 0.

common_visible_process: None. The canvases are static renderings of the generated topology; generic clock progression is not a visible Branch Repair process and is not consumed by the mechanic or grader.

pre_run.reason: At level 1, repair_count is missing_joins plus false_joins, namely 2. The grader requires a successful merge and split, followed by post-edit inspections, before certification. There is no autonomous outcome phase that can complete without those outcome-affecting repair events, so no instance satisfies the specified pre-run pattern; no percentage is reported.

source_evidence.claim: The exact assigned level-1 profile is two fibres, six segments per fibre, one missing join, one false join, seven slices, and crossing density 0.35; full interaction is implemented, with play_time_seconds 180, observation_window_ms 0, and one frame per observation.
The runner exposes a zero-millisecond observation window and one frame, while the environment declares mouse and keyboard action types and synchronous execution.
Controlled task conditions are copied into the task before generation, and branch_repair is dispatched to the incubator generator without a task-time state transition.

The generator selects the supplied difficulty and interaction, constructs fixed seeded nodes and initial/true/missing/false edges, sets repair_count to missing plus false joins, and returns static public and grading state.

The full UI hides simplified buttons, renders linked slices and a mesh, and mutates focus, camera, edges, or seeds only from scroll, pointer, click, and button handlers; no timer, animation loop, clock read, or autonomous update exists.
The mechanic CSS supplies static layout, cursor, hover, and disabled-button styling; it defines no animation or timed transition that could change task state.

The grader replays the submitted event transcript from the static initial graph, requires visible linked-view inspections after every merge/split, requires repair_actions to equal repair_count, and contains no clock or autonomous advancement.
Verification loads the exported result and Branch Repair grader and grades the submitted topology; it does not introduce time-dependent outcome logic.

The shared runtime can run or pause a generic task clock and timers, but those facilities are external plumbing; Branch Repair does not register a timer, animation frame, or clock-dependent state update.

The local solver uses private ground truth and performs direct UI edits with only post-action settling waits; this is implementation evidence and shows no autonomous outcome phase, not a screenshot-only solution claim.
